# ug-lua-llm agent reference

ug-lua-llm is a dependency-light Lua 5.1–5.4 client for OpenAI, Claude, Gemini,
Grok, Groq, OpenRouter, Ollama, DeepSeek, Mistral, and arbitrary
OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoints.

## Install and import

    luarocks install ug-lua-llm

To work against the source, or to try an unreleased change, clone the
repository and run `luarocks make ug-lua-llm-0.3.0-1.rockspec` instead.

    local llm = require "ug-lua-llm"
    local client = llm.new("openai", {
      api_key = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"),
      model = "gpt-5.6-terra",
    })

Supported provider names: openai, claude, gemini, grok, groq, openrouter,
ollama, deepseek, mistral, openai-compatible.

For custom endpoints prefer:

    local client = llm.openai_compatible({
      base_url = "http://localhost:8000/v1",
      model = "my-model",
      api_key = os.getenv("LLM_API_KEY"), -- optional
      headers = {},                       -- optional
      capabilities = { streaming = true, tools = false, models = true },
    })

For local Ollama use `llm.new("ollama", { model = "llama3.2" })`; its default
base URL is http://localhost:11434/v1 and authentication is optional.

## Core contract

Messages are `{ role = "system"|"user"|"assistant"|"tool", content = ... }`.
Every operation returns `result, err, details`. On failure result is nil, err is
human-readable, and optional details describes kind, provider, status, code,
retryability, safe headers, and sanitized body.

Normalized responses expose these fields where available: text, tool_calls,
usage, model, finish_reason, provider, raw. Do not parse provider wire formats
when a normalized field exists. Use raw only for provider-specific data.

text is always a string, never nil. A model that stops before producing content
returns "" with finish_reason "length"; check finish_reason to tell an empty
answer from a truncated one. finish_reason is a string or nil and tool_calls is
a table or nil. JSON null never reaches these fields.

raw is the untouched provider payload, so JSON null is preserved there as the
backend's sentinel, which is truthy in Lua. Test it with
`require("ug-lua-llm.utils.json").is_null(value)` rather than `if value then`;
`JSON.value(value)` returns nil for null and the value otherwise.

Client methods:

- chat(messages, options)
- complete(prompt, options)
- chat_with_tools(messages, tools, options)
- stream_chat(messages, callback, options)
- stream_complete(prompt, callback, options)
- stream_chat_with_tools(messages, tools, callback, options)
- list_models(options)
- capabilities()
- response(input, options): OpenAI Responses only
- interaction(input, options): Gemini Interactions only

Streaming callbacks receive `(delta, full)`. Prefer `delta.content` or
`delta.text`. Deltas may also carry tool_calls, finish_reason, provider, raw.

Tool definitions use `{ name, description, parameters = <JSON Schema> }`.
Parse calls with `llm.Tool.parse_tool_calls(response)`. Each parsed call has id,
name, decoded arguments when valid, type, and raw. Use `llm.ToolRegistry` for
handler registration and automatic execution.

`ToolRegistry.process_response(client, response, messages, callback, options)`
executes the calls and continues the conversation until the model stops asking
for tools. Pass `options.tools` so the follow-up can request a second tool after
seeing the first result; without it the exchange ends after one round.
`options.max_tool_rounds` defaults to 8, and a response that hits the cap
carries `tool_rounds_exhausted = true` plus `tool_pending`, the calls it stopped.
The final response reports the whole exchange rather than only the turn that
answered: `tool_calls` (every call requested across every round), `tool_results`
(every one that ran, each with ok and error), `tool_rounds`, and `messages`, the
conversation ready to continue. `options.on_tool` is called per dispatch.
There is no default temperature; a value present is one the caller chose, and it
is sent as given rather than stripped for models that may refuse it. The bundled `get_weather` and
`calculator` are opt-in since 0.3.0: call
`ToolRegistry.register_standard_tools()` before `ToolRegistry.collection`
resolves them.

Embeddings: `llm.Embeddings.new(provider, config):embed(input, options)` supports
OpenAI, Gemini, Mistral, Ollama, and DeepSeek.

## Reasoning

Use the `reasoning` option: false or "none" to minimize, "low", "medium",
"high", or true. It is translated per provider, and asking for less reasoning
never turns a working request into an error: where a model refuses the control
the request is retried without it. `response.reasoning_applied` is a boolean
whenever a level was asked for and nil when none was, so it is true on
compliance and false both when the control was refused and when the provider
has none.
`response.usage.reasoning_tokens` reports what thinking cost.
`client:capabilities().reasoning_control` is "effort", "budget" (may refuse a
zero budget), "opt_in" (off unless asked), or false.

Reasoning is spent from the same allowance as the reply, so a small max_tokens
can be consumed entirely before content is produced.

## Structured output

Pass a JSON Schema as `json_schema` and read `response.parsed` for the decoded
object; `response.text` still holds the raw JSON document. One schema works for
every provider. A model that refuses a schema falls back to plain JSON mode and
then to an ordinary reply, so check `response.structured_applied` before
trusting the shape. `client:capabilities().structured_output` is "responses",
"chat", "schema", "tool", or false.

## Provider-specific fields

Anything without a normalized option goes in `request_options`, which is merged
into the generated payload. Nested containers are merged rather than replaced,
so `request_options = { generationConfig = { ... } }` reaches Gemini without
discarding the fields the client generates.

## Safe implementation rules

- Check errors; do not assume a response exists.
- Do not log keys, Authorization headers, payload secrets, or `.env` contents.
- Inspect `client:capabilities()` before selecting optional features.
- Treat custom endpoint capabilities as declarations, then run
  `LLM_BASE_URL=... LLM_MODEL=... lua scripts/conformance.lua` to verify them.
- Pass model explicitly when reproducibility matters.
- Keep `/v1` in common Ollama and OpenAI-compatible base URLs.
- Use `lua scripts/doctor.lua` when installed rocks cannot be required.

See docs/index.md for human documentation, examples/README.md for runnable
programs, and CHANGELOG.md for what changed between releases.
